"Bituin ng Mindanao" is a tribute song honoring Rene Clert “Bobet” Baterbonia, a young student-athlete from Talacogon, Agusan del Sur, who was a Palarong Pambansa MVP, led the Davao Region to its first basketball title, and played for the Ateneo Blue Eagles before dying in a drowning incident in Aurora on June 8, 2026. The song has faced ridicule due to Rene’s mother Rovelyn Baterbonia’s actions, including publicly requesting financial donations instead of gifts for the 100th-day commemoration to fund legal costs, selling signed merchandise before his death, and rejecting public apologies from Ateneo officials, which critics say have shifted focus from his legacy to financial concerns and drawn negative attention.
"Bituin ng Mindanao" is a tribute song dedicated to the memory of [[Rene Clert “Bobet” Baterbonia|Rene Clert “Bobet” Baterbonia]], a promising young student-athlete from Talacogon, Agusan del Sur. Baterbonia was a Palarong Pambansa MVP who led the Davao Region to its first-ever basketball title before being recruited to play for the Ateneo Blue Eagles. He tragically passed away in a drowning incident during a team-building activity in Aurora on June 8, 2026. The song honors his legacy as an inspiration to the youth of Mindanao.
The tribute song has gradually become an object of ridicule because of Rene's mother's actions. Some critics argue that her actions have shifted the focus from his legacy to financial matters, which has fueled negative sentiment. The primary points of contention include: (1) **Financial Requests:** Rovelyn Baterbonia publicly requested financial donations instead of material gifts for her son's 100th-day commemoration to help fund their legal battle, which some perceived as capitalizing on his death. (2) **Merchandise Sales:** She addressed accusations of profiting from his passing by explaining that the family had been selling signed keychains and jerseys even before he died to support their household. (3) **Public Disputes:** Her vocal rejection of apologies from Ateneo officials and public demands for accountability, while seen by many as a mother's grief, have also drawn backlash from those who feel the ongoing public dispute overshadows his memory.
